_notes: Parameters derived from ABS Household Expenditure Survey 2021-22. consumption_rate = proportion of after-tax income that is spent (vs saved). gst_coverage = proportion of total spending that falls on GST-applicable goods and services (food staples, health, education, rent, financial services are GST-exempt). Source: ABS Cat. 6530.0, Treasury modelling.
_formula: gst_per_employee = after_tax_income * consumption_rate * gst_coverage * gst_rate / (1 + gst_rate)
_note_formula: We divide by (1 + gst_rate) because retail prices are GST-inclusive; the GST component = price * rate/(1+rate) = price * 10/110

low.label: Low income (< $40k gross)
low.notes: Low-income households spend almost all income and a higher proportion on food/essentials which are GST-exempt, but also proportionally more on fast food, clothing, household goods which are taxable.

low_mid.label: Lower-middle income ($40k–$60k gross)
low_mid.notes: Retail, hospitality and entry-level service workers.

high.label: High income (> $130k gross)
high.notes: High-income earners save more and spend proportionally more on GST-exempt categories: private health insurance, overseas travel, financial services, private school fees.
